items.evidence: Google Maps listing found for 'Café Le Vent' on Köpenicker Str. 44 with 4.6 stars from 321 reviews, opening hours and 94 photos. But no phone number is listed, and the website field points to a Facebook page with no posts since March 2021.
items.why: Most new customers find a café on Google Maps first. A phone number and a working link are what turn a look into a visit.

items.evidence: No website found. The Google listing links only to facebook.com/LeVentCoffee, and search results are only Google Maps, Yelp, Uber Eats and review directories.
items.why: A one-page site is the one place you control: menu, hours, address and a way to contact you, without depending on other platforms.

items.evidence: No website exists, so there is no Impressum or privacy notice of your own. The only legal notice found is on the Uber Eats listing.
items.why: German law requires an Impressum and a privacy page on any business site. Missing them can lead to warning letters and fines.

items.evidence: Three different phone numbers and three versions of the opening hours appear across Google, Apple Maps, Yelp, OpenStreetMap and directories. A Google review from April 2025 says the café was listed as open but was closed.
items.why: When hours or phone numbers differ between platforms, customers show up to a closed door or call a dead line, and Google ranks the listing lower.

items.evidence: There is no website to check, so there is nothing that works on a phone yet.
items.why: Most people searching for a café nearby are on their phone. A site that is hard to read on mobile is almost the same as no site.

items.evidence: Only 1 of 321 Google reviews has an owner reply, from 2019. Five 1–2 star reviews from 5–6 September 2026 about rude staff have no reply, including one in Turkish that asks the owner to get in touch.
items.why: Replying shows future customers that someone cares, and it is the cheapest way to soften a bad review.

items.evidence: No ordering, booking or menu link on the Google listing. The Uber Eats listing has the full menu, but delivery is switched off.
items.why: An online order or pre-order link lets people buy from you when nobody has time to answer the phone.

items.evidence: Instagram account @cafe_le_vent found with 242 followers and 6 posts, but the last post is from 16 May 2023. The Facebook page (118 followers) has had no posts since March 2021.
items.why: One active channel keeps regulars informed about specials and gives new customers a feel for the place.

items.evidence: OpenStreetMap and Apple Maps list cash, Maestro and contactless payment including Apple Pay.
items.why: Many guests, especially tourists, no longer carry cash. Card and contactless payment avoids lost sales at the counter.

items.evidence: A digital stamp card through gobonki started in June 2026 (gobonki's Instagram post). No newsletter or WhatsApp list was found.
items.why: A list of regulars you can message directly is the cheapest way to fill a quiet Tuesday or announce something new.

items.evidence: Cannot be checked from the web. Ask the owner how they handle messages and common questions.
items.why: An AI helper can answer 'Are you open on Sunday?' and draft replies to messages, saving time every day.

items.evidence: Cannot be checked from the web. Ask the owner how they write invoices and track expenses.
items.why: A simple tool keeps receipts and invoices in one place, so tax time is hours instead of days.
